ECE 6390

Satellite PSK and APSK constellations

From the figure to the concept

Fig. 1 shows how the DVB-S2 constellation families trade symbol loading against noise separation and amplifier constraints.

The satellite lecture uses QPSK, 8PSK, 16APSK and 32APSK as a sequence of larger alphabets. They map two, three, four and five coded bits per symbol. At equal symbol rate, a larger alphabet increases coded throughput; at equal average energy, packing more alternatives generally demands a cleaner received signal.

PSK places every symbol on one radius. APSK uses several radii and several phases:16APSK contains 4 inner and 12 outer points; 32APSK contains 4+12+16. The figure normalizes the mean squared point radius to 1 for equally likely symbols. Its ring-radius ratios are explicitly illustrative, not a chosen standard MODCOD.

A satellite high-power amplifier can compress large envelope values to improve power efficiency. Ring structure limits amplitude levels to a few groups but does not eliminate nonlinear distortion. AM/AM changes amplitude; AM/PM changes phase. The existing amplifier-and-backoff topic explores a declared limiter model rather than predicting a real hardware BER.

Equal symbol-center radii do not establish constant envelope between symbols after pulse shaping. A receiver still needs carrier and timing synchronization, distortion estimation and appropriate decision boundaries. Satellite rain fading can favor a smaller constellation or a lower coding rate as link margin falls.

Example

At 5 Msym/s, 8PSK maps 15 Mbit/s of coded labels and 32APSK maps 25 Mbit/s. With an effective rate 3/4 and no further overhead, those correspond to 11.25 and 18.75 Mbit/s of information. These arithmetic rates supply no BER guarantee.

Practice

1. How many points belong to the outermost ring of the 32APSK family illustrated here?

Keep the total 32 and the inner 4+12.

Sixteen points lie on the outermost ring. The full ring populations are 4+12+16.

2. Why can a one-ring PSK constellation still show peaks after filtering?

Follow the continuous transition between two symbol-center points.

Pulse shaping superposes time-shifted pulses during transitions. The continuous envelope can vary even though the allowed symbol-center coordinates share one radius.
